label: Dreischulte 73: Full blood count more than 12 weeks ago during leflunomide treatment
title: Full blood count more than 12 weeks ago during leflunomide treatment
statement: Patient treated with leflunomide - had no FBC check in the last 12 weeks

plain_summary: The 2012 criterion flags a gap of more than 12 weeks since the last full blood count during treatment with leflunomide.

needs_facts.what: Full blood count (FBC) in the 12 weeks up to the latest leflunomide supply
needs_facts.meets: Confirmed no completed full blood count on the latest leflunomide supply date or in the preceding 84 days.

options.words: Confirmed no completed FBC on the supply date or in the preceding 84 days
A completed FBC was done on the supply date or in the preceding 84 days

rule_for_models: At the latest Group A leflunomide supply, regardless of indication or course length, give no finding if a completed full blood count was collected on that date or in the preceding 84 days (12 weeks), using the test collection date rather than a later note date. If dated monitoring evidence confirms that no full blood count was completed in that window, report a finding and cite the latest leflunomide supply and the line confirming the last collection date or the absence of a completed count. If a leflunomide supply is present and monitoring in that window is unknown, report only a possible finding, cite the latest supply and say that confirmation of the latest completed full blood count is missing.
cannot_be_seen: A pharmacy record can omit tests done elsewhere. An old report alone cannot establish the latest test date. A test order does not show that blood was collected.
ask_the_gp: Could we confirm the latest completed full blood count and review the monitoring interval appropriate for this person's leflunomide treatment?
